title: Grieving the Holy Spirit
definition: Grieving the Holy Spirit is the sorrowful offense believers bring against the Spirit through sin, bitterness, corrupt speech, and resistance to His holy work.
summary: Believers can grieve the Spirit by resisting holiness and love.
christFocus: Jesus gives the Spirit to form His people in truth and love, not bitterness and corruption.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Because the Spirit is a Person, He can be grieved. Sin is not merely rule-breaking; it offends the holy God who dwells with His people.

Ephesians connects grieving the Spirit with corrupt speech, bitterness, anger, slander, malice, and lack of forgiveness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Some believers treat sin casually because they forget the Spirit personally dwells in them. This doctrine matters because sin affects fellowship with God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask where your speech, bitterness, or hidden sin is resisting the Spirit's work. Repent and return to kindness, forgiveness, and holiness.
